metadataVO.title: 中国山地不同气候区土壤剖面多元素综合数据集
metadataVO.titleEn: Multi-element dataset of soil profiles across climatic zones in China’s mountains
metadataVO.description: 山地生态系统作为全球生物多样性的热点区域和生物地球化学循环的关键调节器，正面临着全球变化加剧所带来的日益严峻的威胁。尽管其生态功能极为重要，但目前对于山地生态系统中土壤元素分布的大尺度、系统化数据的缺乏，严重制约了我们对多种元素间相互作用及其对生态系统功能调控机制的深入理解。为填补这一关键知识空白，本研究构建了一个覆盖中国30个山地生态系统的大陆尺度土壤元素浓度数据集。该数据集覆盖了热带、亚热带、暖温带、温带和寒温带五大气候区，并对有机层（O层）、表层矿质层（A层）和母质层（C层）三种不同土层的样品进行了采集与分析。通过对24种元素的定量测定，包括主要营养元素（例如磷、钾、钙、镁）、微量金属元素（例如铁、钼、铜、锌）以及潜在有毒元素（例如镉、铬、铅、锑），本研究为土壤元素的多维度分析提供了丰富的基础数据。同时，为支持地球系统综合分析，数据集还同步提供样点环境变量信息，包括气候因子（温度、降水量、干燥指数）、植被指数（NDVI）、土壤理化性质（pH、含水率、容重）、大气氮沉降水平和化学风化指数等。数据分析揭示了土壤元素在土壤剖面中的显著垂直分异规律：有机层中生物元素的富集现象明显，而深层土壤则以矿物元素为主导。此外，沿纬度、经度及海拔梯度的空间分布模式进一步印证了气候与地质条件对土壤元素组成的协同塑造作用。数据集从空间和垂直两个维度描绘了山地土壤元素的分布特征，为深入理解土壤中多元素循环过程中气候、土壤和生物因子之间的复杂耦合机制提供了基础数据支持。该数据集具有广泛的应用前景，可用于改进生物地球化学模型、评估山地生态系统的土壤质量与健康状况、分析不同环境梯度下的元素计量关系，以及追踪敏感山地系统中养分与污染物的来源和归趋。通过促进跨学科、多尺度的研究合作，该数据集不仅深化了我们对山地生态系统应对全球变化能力的基础认知，还为未来的环境监测和管理提供了坚实的数据基础。

metadataVO.nameOfSubmittedPaper: Multi-element dataset of soil profiles across climatic zones in China’s mountains

metadataWordVO.title: Multi-element dataset of soil profiles across climatic zones in China’s mountains
metadataWordVO.description: Mountain ecosystems, as global biodiversity hotspots and critical regulators of biogeochemical cycles, are increasingly vulnerable to accelerating global changes. Despite their ecological significance, the lack of large-scale, comprehensive datasets on soil element distributions has hindered our understanding of how multiple soil elements interact and regulate ecosystem functions under rapid environmental shifts. To address this critical knowledge gap, we present a continental-scale dataset of soil element concentrations from 30 mountain ecosystems across China, spanning five major climatic zones (tropical, subtropical, warm temperate, temperate, and cold temperate regions) and three pedogenetically distinct soil horizons (organic (O), surface mineral (A), and parent material (C) horizons). This dataset encompasses quantitative measurements of 24 elements, including major nutrients (e.g., phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium), trace metals (e.g., iron, molybdenum, copper, zinc), and toxic elements (e.g., cadmium, chromium, lead, antimony). To support integrated Earth system analyses, the dataset is accompanied by key site-specific environmental variables, including climate parameters (temperature, precipitation, aridity index), normalized difference vegetation index, soil physicochemical properties (pH, moisture, bulk density), atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and chemical weathering index. The dataset reveals significant vertical stratification in element distributions, with organic horizon enriched in biogenic elements, and deeper horizons dominated by lithogenic components. Spatial patterns along latitudinal, longitudinal, and altitudinal gradients underscore the influence of climate and geology on soil chemistry. This dataset offers a unique, continental-scale characterization of soil elemental distribution with integrated spatial and vertical dimensions, providing a holistic view of soil biogeochemistry in mountain environments. It serves as an invaluable resource for disentangling the complex interplay of climatic, edaphic, and biological factors regulating soil element cycling. Researchers can utilize this dataset to: improve biogeochemical models, assess soil quality and ecosystem health under rapid environmental change, investigate elemental stoichiometry across environmental gradients, and identify the sources and fates of nutrients and pollutants in vulnerable mountain systems. By enabling cross-disciplinary investigations at an unparalleled scale, this dataset advances our fundamental understanding of mountain ecosystem resilience and provides a robust baseline for future environmental monitoring.
metadataWordVO.instructions:
Data file name: The comprehensive dataset of soil elements in Chinese mountain is stored in Excel, and the file name is "Soil dataset. xlsx".
Usage Instructions: The data can be opened directly using Excel. Abbreviations used in the dataset are explained in the accompanying document "Description of the dataset.docx".

For re-posting (second or multiple releases) data, the author must also indicate the source of the original data.
